title: Moving to Angular
summary: Map each AngularJS idea you learned to its modern Angular counterpart.

quiz.q: Which modern Angular feature replaces an AngularJS controller together with its HTML?
quiz.explain: A component is a class plus a template, so it covers what `ng-controller` and its markup did, and it gets its own tag.

quiz.q: Complete the modern template that replaces `<li ng-repeat="s in students">`.
quiz.explain: The built-in control flow block is `@for (item of items; track item.id)`. The `track` expression tells Angular how to recognise each item.

quiz.q: In AngularJS you wrote `$scope.count = 0`. How do you hold the same value in a modern component?
options: A class field, or a signal such as `count = signal(0)`
quiz.explain: Data lives in fields of the component class. A signal wraps a value so Angular knows exactly which parts of the page to update when it changes.

quiz.q: Which AngularJS idea maps to an `@Injectable()` class obtained with `inject()` or a constructor parameter?
quiz.explain: Dependency injection survived. Your factory becomes an injectable class, and `inject(StudentService)` replaces naming it in the function parameters.

quiz.q: Which are true about the move away from AngularJS? Pick all that apply.
options: AngularJS code runs unchanged in modern Angular
quiz.explain: Interpolation, conditions and formatting all continue in new forms: `{{ }}`, `@if` and pipes. AngularJS code does not run unchanged. Migration is a rewrite, often done step by step.
